fullPassage:
[1번] People sometimes worry that a bank will run out of money. So they all panic and try to withdraw their money. This is called a bank run. In some cases, it can cause a bank to go bankrupt. The reason for this is that most banks keep a limited amount of money in their safes. They do this for security purposes. The amount is only a small percentage of the total deposits made by customers. Therefore, if a bank run occurs, the bank must find a way to increase the amount of cash they have on hand. One way that they can do this is by selling their assets. These sales must be done quickly, so the price of the assets is likely to be much lower than normal. This can cause even more customer anxiety, leading to increased withdrawals.

[2번] Although being ill is quite serious, some trips to the hospital now include unexpected laughter. Healthcare workers have been dressing up like clowns to help patients relax and reduce the stress staying in the hospital can cause. Evidence suggests the laughter these medical clowns create is as effective as some medication. In one experiment, researchers sent clowns to entertain children being prepared for surgery. One group of kids spent about half an hour with a clown, while a second group of children received a sedative instead. The kids who met with clowns showed the same reduction in anxiety as those who were given the sedative. It is believed that medical clowns could also be used to help kids with autism and young burn victims in need of painful bandage-changing.

[3번] In the 1950s, biologists observed chimpanzees that weren't biologically related sharing meat. They struggled to understand why animals that aren't part of the same family help one another. Today, it is believed that the answer is related to game theory. To understand this concept better, consider the following situation. Tournaments were once held by a political scientist in which computer programs competed against each other. Each program had a specific strategy that it followed when encountering an opponent — cooperating with it, backing down from it, and so on. A strategy emerged over time that was more successful than others: start by being cooperative, and then simply copy your opponents' behavior. In other words, if they cooperate, I cooperate. If they stop sharing with me, I stop sharing with them. The behavior we observe in the animal kingdom that is similar to this is called reciprocity. The chimpanzees share food with others because they believe the other will return the favor.

[4번] Baarle is a small border village where areas of Belgian land are scattered within the surrounding Dutch territory. To make things more confusing, there are some Belgian areas within the Dutch territory that contain smaller Dutch properties. It is one of only a few places in the world that have such a complicated border. In 1995, the Belgian and Dutch governments decided to clearly mark the unusual border with a line on the ground. If the border line runs through the middle of buildings such as houses and cafes, it cuts them in half, and each part belongs to a different country. Which country do you live in if your house is divided by this line? This is determined by where your front door is! So if the Dutch annoyed you last week, all you have to do is move your front door to relocate to Belgium.

[5번] The sit-in movement was part of the struggle for racial equality in the US. Its goal was to end the forced separation of races in public places. One of the most important events of this movement was the moment when some African American college students sat in a segregated section of a restaurant in North Carolina. They were told to leave, but they protested by remaining in their seats. This was not the first sit-in of the civil rights movement, but it led to a series of similar protests. During them, protesters occupied seats in places where races were segregated, including restaurants and libraries. They refused to move unless they were either served or arrested. Many establishments decided to end their practice of racial segregation rather than deal with more protests. These sit-ins helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which officially ended segregation in public places.

[6번] Insomnia sufferers face a vicious cycle. First, they fail to sleep well for a few nights in a row, and then they begin to experience stress about their lack of sleep. This stress, in turn, leads to further trouble sleeping. While many patients feel medication is the only remedy for their problem, doctors disagree. They believe that a psychological condition is often responsible for insomnia. This condition can be treated with cognitive behavioral therapy, which focuses on changing the way these people think about insomnia, thereby enabling a change in behavior. The therapy involves showing patients that they can still be healthy even if they fail to get a good night's sleep once in a while.

[7번] Grace Hopper was born in New York in 1906. She showed an interest in mechanics at an early age, often taking apart appliances and putting them back together. She earned degrees in mathematics and physics at Vassar College and later received a PhD in mathematics from Yale. Upon graduating, she returned to Vassar as a professor. Following the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941, which caused the US to enter World War II, Hopper joined the military. In 1944, she was assigned to a computer project at Harvard University. Her team helped create an early version of an electronic computer. After the war, she took part in the creation of UNIVAC, the first all-electronic digital computer. She eventually reached the rank of commander and was recognized internationally for her work with computers. In 1973, she became the first woman to be named a distinguished fellow of the British Computer Society.

[8번] Mount Vesuvius is a volcano in Italy that had been inactive for hundreds of years until August 24, 79 A.D., when it suddenly erupted. The eruption began in the morning, as rock and lava began to be expelled at an amazing rate of 1.5 million tons per second. The sky darkened and about six inches of ash fell to the ground each hour. The lava started to flow around midnight, and the next morning a cloud of toxic gas reached Pompeii, where around 20,000 people lived. At the time, the region was a popular resort spot, with many tourists. Most of the people who did not leave at the start of the eruption were buried alive in rock and ash. In the end, it is believed that approximately 16,000 people died.

[9번] Whenever people on ships use a radio to call for help, they use the word "mayday." But what does it mean? The word was actually selected by a British man named Frederick Mockford in the 1920s. He chose it because it sounds like the French term m'adier, which means "help me." According to standard procedure, the word is to be said three times in a row so that it won't be mistaken for something similar. After this, important information should be given, such as the name and location of the ship. Sometimes, however, one ship will make a mayday call for another ship in trouble. This is called a "mayday relay." It is done when a ship in danger is unable to contact rescuers. A ship hearing the original call may choose to repeatedly perform a mayday relay until help is on the way. This is because when a mayday call is sent, whoever receives it is expected to help out however they can.

[10번] Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.

① offered a free meal(무료 식사 제공): 식사 제공 이야기는 없어요.

② told to leave(떠나라는 말을 들은): 떠나라는 요구를 받고도 'but' 자리에 남아 항의했다는 대조가 자연스러워요 ←정답

④ given an apology(사과를 받은): 사과 이야기는 없어요.
det.tip: but(그러나) + 자리에 남아 저항 → 앞은 반대인 '떠나라는 요구(told to leave)'

questions.passage: Insomnia sufferers face a vicious cycle. First, they fail to sleep well for a few nights in a row, and then they begin to experience stress about their lack of sleep. This stress, in turn, leads to further trouble sleeping. While many patients feel medication is the only remedy for their problem, doctors disagree. They believe that a psychological condition is often responsible for insomnia. This condition can be treated with cognitive behavioral therapy, which focuses on changing the way these people think about insomnia, thereby enabling a change in behavior. The therapy involves showing patients that they can still be healthy even if they fail to get a good night's sleep once in a while.
questions.stem: 불면증 환자는 수면 부족에 대한 스트레스 때문에 오히려 잠을 더 못 자는 악순환을 겪는다.

det.korean: 본문 'stress ... leads to further trouble sleeping(스트레스가 더 심한 수면 문제로 이어진다)'과 일치 → T
det.analysis: 본문에서 불면증 환자는 잠을 못 자면 수면 부족에 대한 스트레스를 겪고, 그 스트레스가 다시 '더 심한 수면 문제로 이어진다(leads to further trouble sleeping)'고 했어요. 진술의 '악순환'과 일치해요 → T ←정답
det.tip: 스트레스 → 수면 문제 심화 = 악순환. 일치(T)

questions.passage: Grace Hopper was ①<u>born</u> in New York in 1906. She ②<u>showed</u> an interest in mechanics at an early age, often taking apart appliances and putting them back together. She earned degrees in mathematics and physics at Vassar College and later received a PhD in mathematics from Yale. Upon graduating, she returned to Vassar as a professor. Following the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941, which caused the US to enter World War II, Hopper joined the military. In 1944, she was ③<u>assigned</u> to a computer project at Harvard University. Her team ④<u>helped creating</u> an early version of an electronic computer. After the war, she took part in the creation of UNIVAC, the first all-electronic digital computer. She eventually reached the rank of commander and was recognized internationally for her work with computers. In 1973, she became the first woman to be named a distinguished fellow of the British Computer Society.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: helped creating → helped create (help + 동사원형/to부정사)
det.analysis:
① born: 'was born in New York' 수동태(be + 과거분사) — 적절
② showed: 'She showed an interest' 과거시제 — 적절
③ assigned: 'she was assigned to a computer project' 수동태 — 적절
④ helped creating: help는 목적어로 동사원형(또는 to부정사)을 취하므로 helped create가 옳음 ←정답
det.tip: help + 동사원형/to부정사. help creating은 불가 → helped (to) create

questions.passage: Mount Vesuvius is a volcano in Italy that had been inactive for hundreds of years until August 24, 79 A.D., when it suddenly erupted. The eruption began in the morning, as rock and lava began to be expelled at an amazing rate of 1.5 million tons per second. The sky darkened and about six inches of ash fell to the ground each hour. The lava started to flow around midnight, and the next morning a cloud of toxic gas reached Pompeii, where around 20,000 people lived. At the time, the region was a popular resort spot, with many tourists. Most of the people who did not leave at the start of the eruption were buried alive in rock and ash. In the end, it is believed that approximately 16,000 people died.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 'about six inches of ash fell to the ground each hour' — 일치
det.analysis:
① 폭발 전 수백 년간 활동하지 않았음(inactive) — 불일치
② 용암은 자정 무렵(around midnight) 흐르기 시작 — 불일치
③ 화산재가 시간당 약 6인치씩 떨어짐 ←정답(일치)
④ 떠나지 않은 사람 대부분은 산 채로 묻힘 — 불일치
det.tip: about six inches of ash fell to the ground each hour = 시간당 6인치

ch: 베수비오 화산은 폭발 전 수백 년간 활발히 분출하고 있었다.

questions.passage: Whenever people on ships use a radio to call for help, they use the word "mayday." But what does it mean? The word was actually selected by a British man named Frederick Mockford in the 1920s. He chose it because it sounds like the French term m'adier, which means "help me." According to standard procedure, the word is to be said three times in a row so that it won't be mistaken for something similar. After this, important information should be given, such as the name and location of the ship. Sometimes, however, one ship will make a mayday call for another ship in trouble. This is called a "mayday relay." It is done when a ship in danger is unable to contact rescuers. A ship hearing the original call may choose to repeatedly perform a mayday relay until help is on the way. This is because when a mayday call is sent, whoever receives it is expected to help out however they can.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 핵심: mayday의 유래(프랑스어 유래·영국인이 선택) + 사용법(세 번 반복, 릴레이, 도움 기대)
det.analysis:
① 라디오 기술: 도입 배경일 뿐 주제 아님
② 프랑스어 위상: m'adier는 유래 설명일 뿐
③ 여러 방식 비교: 본문은 mayday 하나만 다룸
④ mayday의 유래와 사용 방법 ←정답
det.tip: 전체 흐름: 단어의 유래 → 말하는 방법 → 릴레이 사용

ch: 선박 라디오 통신 기술의 역사적 발전 과정
여러 조난 신호 방식의 장단점 비교 분석

questions.passage: Although new technologies often seem to save us time and money, these savings vanish into thin air when we do a thorough cost analysis. For example, when email was first introduced, it changed the way we communicate. Whatever the message is and however long it may be, you can quickly type it out and send it anywhere for free. But there are other factors that must be considered. Spam emails need to be filtered out, and we all receive many messages that are unimportant but still must be read. This can be a time-consuming process. And when calculating the cost savings that email brings, you should also consider the cost of your computer and smartphone, as well as the time it takes for your software to update. Roughly, it can be estimated that each email you send costs you one dollar, which is as much as an old-fashioned letter.
questions.stem: 새로운 기술은 겉으로 보기에 우리의 시간과 돈을 절약해 주는 것처럼 보인다.

det.korean: 'new technologies often seem to save us time and money' → T
det.analysis: 첫 문장에서 새로운 기술이 흔히 우리의 시간과 돈을 아껴 주는 것처럼 '보인다(seem to save)'고 했어요. 겉보기에는 그렇다는 뜻이라 진술과 일치해요 → T ← 정답
det.tip: seem to save = 절약해 주는 것처럼 보인다

questions.stem: 위 글에서 며칠 밤 연속으로 잘 자지 못한 뒤 환자들이 겪기 시작하는 것을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (6단어, 영어로)

det.korean: stress about their lack of sleep = 수면 부족에 대한 스트레스
det.analysis: 본문 'they begin to experience stress about their lack of sleep(그들은 수면 부족에 대한 스트레스를 겪기 시작한다)'에서 며칠 밤 잘 자지 못한 뒤 환자들이 겪기 시작하는 것 = stress about their lack of sleep. 명사 stress를 전치사구 about their lack of sleep가 뒤에서 꾸며요.

questions.passage: She eventually reached the rank of commander and was recognized internationally for her work with computers. In 1973, she became the first woman to be named a __________ (distinguish) fellow of the British Computer Society.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: distinguish → distinguished (a distinguished fellow: 저명한 회원, 과거분사가 형용사로 명사 수식)
det.analysis: 동사 distinguish(뛰어나게 하다)를 과거분사 distinguished로 바꿔요. 'a distinguished fellow'는 '저명한(뛰어난) 회원'이라는 뜻으로, 과거분사가 형용사처럼 뒤의 명사 fellow를 꾸며요.
det.tip: 명사 fellow를 꾸미는 형용사 자리 → 과거분사 distinguished(저명한)

questions.stem: 위 글에서, 폭발이 시작될 때 떠나지 않은 사람들이 어떻게 되었는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (3단어, 영어로)

det.korean: were buried alive = 산 채로 묻혔다
det.analysis: 본문 'Most of the people who did not leave at the start of the eruption were buried alive in rock and ash'에서 떠나지 않은 사람들은 산 채로 묻혔어요(were buried alive). were(be동사) + buried(과거분사)의 수동태예요.
det.tip: were + 과거분사 = 수동태. buried alive = 산 채로 묻힌

questions.passage: A ship hearing the original call may choose to repeatedly perform a mayday relay until help is on the way. This is because when a mayday call is __________ (send), whoever receives it is expected to help out however they can.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: send(동사: 보내다) → sent(과거분사: 보내진). 수동태 be + p.p.
det.analysis: send를 과거분사 sent로 바꿔요. 'when a mayday call is sent(메이데이 신호가 보내질 때)'처럼, 주어(a mayday call)가 스스로 보내는 것이 아니라 '보내지는' 대상이므로 수동태 'is + 과거분사(sent)'를 써요. send의 과거분사는 불규칙형 sent예요.
det.tip: be + p.p. = 수동태. send의 과거분사는 sent(불규칙)

questions.stem: 위 글에서 스팸을 걸러내고 중요하지 않은 메시지를 읽는 일을 필자가 무엇이라고 표현했는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (3단어, 영어로)

det.korean: a time-consuming process = 시간이 많이 드는 과정
det.analysis: 본문 'This can be a time-consuming process.'에서, This는 앞 문장(스팸을 걸러내고 불필요한 메시지를 읽는 일)을 가리켜요. 그 일을 'a time-consuming process(시간이 많이 드는 과정)'라고 표현했어요.
det.tip: time-consuming = 시간이 많이 드는. This = 스팸 처리 + 불필요한 메일 읽기
